# 1 Chronicles Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 373r–374v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_006_page_001.jpg, 1CH_006_page_002.jpg, 1CH_006_page_003.jpg, 1CH_006_page_004.jpg

---

**1** The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari. **2** The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. **3** The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

**4** Eleazar was the father of Phinehas; Phinehas of Abishua; **5** Abishua of Bukki; Bukki of Uzzi; **6** Uzzi of Zerahiah; Zerahiah of Meraioth; **7** Meraioth of Amariah; Amariah of Ahitub; **8** Ahitub of Zadok; Zadok of Ahimaaz; **9** Ahimaaz of Azariah; Azariah of Johanan; **10** and Johanan of Azariah — the priest who served in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.

**11** Azariah was the father of Amariah; Amariah of Ahitub; **12** Ahitub of Zadok; Zadok of Shallum; **13** Shallum of Hilkiah; Hilkiah of Azariah; **14** Azariah of Seraiah; and Seraiah of Jehozadak. **15** Jehozadak was taken away when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile under Nebuchadnezzar.

**16** The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari. **17** The sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei. **18** The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. **19** The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans listed by their ancestors.

**20** From Gershom: Libni, then Jahath, Zimmah, **21** Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai. **22** From Kohath: Amminadab, then Korah, Assir, **23** Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir, **24** Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul. **25** The descendants of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth. **26** From Elkanah: Zophai, then Nahath, **27** Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah. **28** The sons of Samuel: Joel the firstborn and Abijah the second.

**29** From Merari: Mahli, then Libni, Shimei, Uzzah, **30** Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah.

**31** These are the men David put in charge of music in the LORD's house after the ark found its resting place. **32** They served with music before the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the LORD's temple in Jerusalem, and they carried out their duties according to the regulations.

**33** Here are those who served, along with their lineage: From the Kohathites — Heman the musician, descended from Joel, Samuel, **34** Elkanah, Jeroham, Eliel, Toah, **35** Zuph, Elkanah, Mahath, Amasai, **36** Elkanah, Joel, Azariah, Zephaniah, **37** Tahath, Assir, Ebiasaph, Korah, **38** Izhar, Kohath, Levi, and Israel.

**39** Heman's colleague Asaph, who stood at his right: Asaph was descended from Berechiah, Shimea, **40** Michael, Baaseiah, Malchijah, **41** Ethni, Zerah, Adaiah, **42** Ethan, Zimmah, Shimei, **43** Jahath, Gershom, and Levi.

**44** On the left stood their fellow Levites, the Merarites: Ethan, descended from Kishi, Abdi, Malluch, **45** Hashabiah, Amaziah, Hilkiah, **46** Amzi, Bani, Shemer, **47** Mahli, Mushi, Merari, and Levi.

**48** The rest of the Levites were assigned to all the other duties of the tabernacle, God's house.

**49** But only Aaron and his descendants made the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and the altar of incense. They alone handled all the work of the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel, following everything that Moses, God's servant, had commanded.

**50** These were the descendants of Aaron: Eleazar, then Phinehas, Abishua, **51** Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, **52** Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub, **53** Zadok, and Ahimaaz.

**54** These were the places where Aaron's descendants lived, assigned to them by lot — the Kohathite clan received the first allotment. **55** They were given Hebron in Judah, with its surrounding pasturelands. **56** But the farmland and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.

**57** Aaron's descendants received these cities of refuge: Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, **58** Hilen, Debir, **59** Ashan, and Beth-shemesh — each with its pasturelands. **60** From the tribe of Benjamin: Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth with their pasturelands — thirteen cities in all for the Aaronic clan.

**61** The remaining Kohathites received ten cities by lot from the half-tribe of Manasseh. **62** The Gershomites received thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan. **63** The Merarites received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

**64** So the Israelites gave these cities and their pasturelands to the Levites. **65** From the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin they assigned the cities listed here by name.

**66** Some Kohathite clans received cities from the tribe of Ephraim. **67** They were given the cities of refuge: Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and Gezer, **68** Jokmeam, Beth-horon, **69** Aijalon, and Gath-rimmon — each with pasturelands.

**70** From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Aner and Bileam with their pasturelands, for the remaining Kohathites.

**71** The Gershomites received from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth with their pasturelands. **72** From Issachar: Kedesh, Daberath, **73** Ramoth, and Anem with their pasturelands. **74** From Asher: Mashal, Abdon, **75** Hukok, and Rehob with their pasturelands. **76** From Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim with their pasturelands.

**77** The remaining Merarites received from Zebulun: Rimmono and Tabor with their pasturelands. **78** From the tribe of Reuben, east of the Jordan near Jericho: Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah, **79** Kedemoth, and Mephaath with their pasturelands. **80** From Gad: Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, **81** Heshbon, and Jazer with their pasturelands.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verses 1-15 — The priestly chain:** Twenty-three links connect Levi to the exile. This is not just genealogy — it is the chain of legitimate authority. Every high priest in Israel's history is accounted for, from Aaron to the man who was carried to Babylon. The Chronicler's post-exilic community needs to know: our priests are authorized.

**Verse 10 — "who served in the temple Solomon built":** The Chronicler interrupts the list to anchor it in space. Among all these names, this Azariah served in *that* building. The genealogy is not abstract — it is connected to the most sacred place on earth.

**Verses 31-47 — Three musicians, three clans:** Heman (center), Asaph (right), Ethan (left) — each traced back through their entire Levitical lineage to Levi himself. These are not performers; they are liturgical officers. Their genealogies are their credentials.

**Verse 49 — "only Aaron and his sons":** The Chronicler draws a sharp line between priests and Levites. The Levites serve the house; the priests serve the altar. This distinction mattered intensely in the post-exilic period, when disputes over priestly authority were common.

**Verses 54-81 — Cities without a homeland:** The Levites received no tribal territory. Instead, they were scattered across all the other tribes — a deliberate theological design. God was their inheritance (cf. Deut 10:9), and their physical distribution ensured every tribe had access to priestly service.

*— PNEUMA*
